Traffic along Cele towards Pako is moving well in both directions. The Cele linked bridge inward Ijesha is also free-flowing with no issues reported on the return journey. Movement through the inner part of Nwachukwu Drive connecting Cele remains smooth in both directions. Ago Palace Road is experiencing encouraging movement along both the inward and outward routes up to Apple Junction. Traffic on Ibeh Road, Apata inward from Transformer Junction to Ilasa Under Bridge service lane, is clear with no impediments in either direction. The inner section of Ire Akari linking Osolo Road is also moving steadily.

However, traffic is slow around Oke Afa, Pako, Kogberegbe, Ile Ibadan, Ishaga College, Omonide, Aye, and Limca Junction inward to Lasutech Roundabout, extending towards Daleko Bridge, due to activities at Daleko Market. Meanwhile, Five Star, Iyana Isolo, and Iyana Itire inward to Ijesha Express, across both the main carriageways and the service lanes, are currently free with no impediments reported.
Oir men are present at important locations ensuring ease of traffic movement.

data.text:
Let me take a short break from aviation to talk about this overlooked transport opportunity The Runway We Refuse to Use.

My first love is aviation ✈️ but reflecting on the Calabar Coastal Road and Railway made me pause: why do we ignore our waterways?

Nigeria has 850 km of coastline and rich rivers, yet interstate marine transport gets no real investment. Roads, rail, and aviation take the spotlight while ferries remain sidelined.

In Asia, ferries are lifelines:
•🇯🇵 Osaka → Kagoshima (12–15 hrs)
•🇵🇭 Manila → Cebu (22 hrs)
•🇮🇩 Java → Batam (long-distance ferries daily)

If they can do it, why can’t we?

A Lagos–Calabar high-speed ferry could take just 8–10 hrs. Imagine boarding at a Lagos jetty at night, stretching out in a cabin, and waking up at sunrise in Calabar no potholes, no checkpoints, no gridlock.

The truth? Waterways are ignored because of policy bias, poor dredging, security fears, and perception. 
But they remain one of our biggest missed opportunities. 

As a transport enthusiast, I see it this way: we’re busy building runways on land and rail tracks across the coast yet ignoring the natural runway God already gave us at sea.

Fast ferries are becoming a reality in East Africa. The question is why not here?

If Asia can move millions by sea, what’s really stopping Nigeria?

#Transport #BlueEconomy #Nigeria #Maritime
